0.22.3 reads QWEN_HOME via getGlobalQwenDir(); 0.14.3 ignores it and reads ~/.qwen. A 0.14.x user with QWEN_HOME exported for any unrelated reason saw ZERO sessions, because both resolvers treated QWEN_HOME as authoritative with no fallback. Discovery, the source descriptor and resume eligibility now share QwenSessionDiscovery.resolvedSessionsRoot and fall back to ~/.qwen/projects when $QWEN_HOME/projects is not a directory. Trigger is one directoryExists check, not an enumeration, because the descriptor applies the same rule inside isAvailable and must not walk the filesystem there.

Third consumer the plan did not account for: QwenResumeEligibility passed 'preference ?? qwenHome' as customRoot, laundering QWEN_HOME through the branch that never falls back. Fixing discovery alone would have listed the ~/.qwen sessions and then marked every one browse-only (supportsResumeLookup=false). It now passes only the preference, and on the fallback path names ~/.qwen explicitly as the QWEN_HOME override rather than inheriting the user's stale export, which 0.22.3 would otherwise honor and resolve wrongly.

validatedRecord gates on type in {user, assistant, tool_result, system} and returns nil otherwise, so a record from a newer writer left NO trace: not mis-bucketed into a catch-all, gone. Now censused and reported as one trailing meta event. Unknown types and unknown subtypes are counted separately because their fates differ - a type is skipped and shown nowhere, a subtype renders as meta with rawJSON intact. Subtype counts are scoped to the active chain so a dead rewind branch cannot warn about content the transcript does not show. Records stay OUT of the chain walk, matching 0.22.3's own validateTranscriptRecord, so leaf selection is unchanged.

0.22.3's KNOWN_RECORD_SUBTYPES (packages/core/src/utils/transcript-records.ts, read from the installed @qwen-code/qwen-code@0.22.3 package) carries 22 subtypes plus the 2 artifact ones. Mirrored into the parser to decide novelty only - it changes how nothing renders. Every one is written with createBaseRecord("system") except goal_runtime and mid_turn_user_message ("user") and realtime_message (the entry's own role), so the system-typed ones already reached the transcript as meta and needed no code.

CORRECTED, and the error was in the dangerous direction. The brief inferred realtime_message was bookkeeping and proposed defaulting it to meta. The writer says otherwise: recordRealtimeConversation emits {...createBaseRecord(entry.role), subtype: 'realtime_message', message: <real text>}, so it is user- or assistant-typed and carries real conversation. Bucketing it to meta would have HIDDEN actual messages. It already renders correctly, so the correct action was no code change.

New in 0.22.3 and absent from the brief's list. type="user" with a real message plus systemPayload.displayText - a user message sent mid-turn, which our parser already renders as conversation and whose displayText the existing payload projection already prefers. Explicitly NOT added to runtimeUserSubtypes: doing so would demote a real message out of the transcript and out of title derivation.

UPSTREAM INCONSISTENCY, recorded so it is not re-derived: 0.22.3 writes subtype 'user_text_elements' (createBaseRecord("system")) but omits it from its own KNOWN_RECORD_SUBTYPES, so upstream's validateTranscriptRecord flags records upstream itself writes with an unknown_record_or_part diagnostic. Ours includes it deliberately - without it every such record would read as novelty on the first real transcript.

Settles the interleaving risk the brief was written around: it does not exist. 0.22.3 writes subagent transcripts through a SEPARATE writer to <projectDir>/subagents/<sessionId>/agent-<agentId>.jsonl, with its own file descriptor, its own lastUuid chain and isSidechain:true on every record. agentId, agentName, agentColor, isSidechain, agentRunId and agentRound exist only there. transcriptLocation accepts only <project>/chats/<id>.jsonl and chats/archive/, so those records can never interleave into a main chain - and are entirely invisible to us. Matches the 'subagent hierarchy' entry already in unsupported_surfaces; supporting it is a new feature, not format drift.

The only one of the five subagent/fork fields that appears in chats/ transcripts: forkedFrom {sessionId, messageUuid}, stamped on every record when a session is forked. Already retained verbatim in each event's rawJSON, which is what capture required, so no code change. Pinned by testForkedFromIsRetainedOnTheRecordItWasWrittenOn.
